newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss shares end down on Wall Street weakness.
newsitem.headline: Swiss shares end down on Wall Street weakness.

text.p: Swiss shares closed lower after strong U.S. May industrial production data led to a fall on Wall Street, dragging most European bourses down with it, dealers said.
"We have a consolidation at a high level, which is normal," one dealer said. He added that the moves on Wall Street in the next few sessions are likely to give the market direction.
The Swiss Market Index (SMI) of leading shares ended off 16.1 points, or 0.3 percent, at 5,345.9 and the Swiss Performance Index (SPI) gave up 6.24 points, or 0.18 percent, to finish at 3,400.56.
Bourse volume stood at 2.54 billion Swiss francs. Trade was reportedly dominated by professionals.
Novartis shares were among the few winners in the blue-chip sector.
Dealers said the stock profited from an analyst presentation which centred on research and development at Novartis' pharma division. The registered shares were up 30 francs to 2,118.

Some switches from Roche certificates to Novartis may have caused a fall in Roche certificates of 105 francs to 12,850, one trader noted. But he added buying may soon resume given the fact Roche was nearly 1,000 francs off this year's highs.
Bearer shares of watchmaker SMH gained eight francs to end at 907. A dealer said the market's view of the stock was becoming more positive.
Insurer Zurich, which was traded ex dividend of 7.20 francs, ended off 11 at 555.
Sulzer, which has recently shot up following detailed information on the IPO of its medical unit, slumped 45 francs, or 3.36 percent, to 1,295.
CS Group continued to fall after its recent rally. The stock yielded 4.50 francs to end at 184.50.
On the Swiss Options and Futures Exchange (Soffex), total options volume reached 105,780 and SMI future volume 11,584 contracts.
